implement.summary:
TERMINATION FOR CONVENIENCE CLAUSE
Software subscription agreement — one-year Term — governed by the law of England and Wales

Clause [•] — Termination for convenience

[•].1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time during the Term by giving the other Party not less than thirty (30) days' written notice of termination. Written notice under this clause [•] may be given by prepaid first-class post or by email to the address (and, for email, the designated recipient) specified in clause [Notices]. Termination in accordance with this clause [•] is not a breach of this Agreement by the Party giving the notice.

[•].2 A notice given under clause [•].1 takes effect on the date it is received by the receiving Party. A notice sent by post is received on the date it is delivered to the receiving Party's notice address in clause [Notices]. A notice sent by email is received on the date it arrives at the receiving Party's designated email address in clause [Notices]. The Termination Date is the date that is thirty (30) days after the date the notice takes effect, or such later date as is specified in the notice, and in either case the Termination Date shall not be later than the last day of the Term.

[•].3 If this Agreement is terminated under clause [•].1, the Supplier shall refund to the Customer the Subscription Fees paid in advance in respect of the unexpired part of the Term. The unexpired part of the Term is the period beginning on the day after the Termination Date and ending on the last day of the Term. The refund shall be calculated on a pro rata daily basis as follows:

Refund = Prepaid Subscription Fees for the Term multiplied by N, divided by D

where N is the number of whole calendar days in the unexpired part of the Term, and D is the number of calendar days in the Term (365, or 366 in a leap year). The refund shall be rounded down to the nearest whole unit of the currency in which the Subscription Fees were paid, and shall be paid to the original payment method used by the Customer within thirty (30) days of the Termination Date.

Which of the three terms each sub-clause carries out

[•].1 — Carries out: "Either party may terminate on thirty days' written notice."
[•].2 — Carries out: "A notice takes effect on the date it is received."
[•].3 — Carries out: "The customer is refunded the prepaid fees for the unexpired part of the term, pro rata."

Drafting notes for the reviewing attorney (jurisdiction: England and Wales)

1. This clause confers a contractual convenience-termination right. Because the Term is a fixed one-year period, the implied right to terminate an unspecified-duration contract on reasonable notice under the Supply of Goods and Services Act 1982, c. 29, s. 14, does not apply; the express right in this clause is therefore the convenience-termination right.

2. The clause is drafted for two business Parties. If the Customer is a consumer, the Consumer Rights Act 2015, c. 15 (Part 2, digital content; Part 3, services) and the Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013, SI 2013/3134, may confer statutory cancellation and refund rights that cannot be excluded by this clause.

3. Defined terms assumed to exist in the host agreement: Agreement, Party, Term, Subscription Fees, Customer, Supplier. Insert the clause number for [•] and the cross-reference for [Notices]. If the host agreement uses different party names (for example Licensor/Licensee), substitute those terms.

4. The refund applies on any convenience termination, whether by the Customer or the Supplier, so that prepaid fees for services not provided are returned. Fees already earned for the period up to and including the Termination Date are retained.

5. Check the host agreement for a minimum-commitment, auto-renewal or minimum-term clause that would conflict with the right to terminate at any time, and check that the Notices clause specifies postal and email addresses and designated recipients.

6. Termination under this clause does not of itself affect rights accrued before the Termination Date; confirm the host agreement's survival and data-return provisions continue to apply after convenience termination.

This draft is for review by a qualified attorney in England and Wales. It is not legal advice.
